Linux dependencies now use one “Update container image” action instead of exposing Find/Open settings steps. An explicit click checks complete committed settings and updates a verified current commit even from an equivalent historical view, preserving the inspected revision and monitoring choices. Unmerged or mismatching choices stop with a specific prerequisite rather than being ignored. VIPM retains exact-target approval; LVPM builds a candidate without activating it.

Linux workflows dispatch the default branch with an optional expected_sha input, validate exactly 40 hexadecimal characters case-insensitively, and reject branch races before checkout, setup, or building with guidance to click again. Every Update request supplies this input; leaving it empty preserves existing manual, push, and schedule behavior. Older installed workflows require a tooling update before dispatch. Duplicate and uncertain requests remain blocked, and page loads or read-only checks never trigger a build. Workflow acceptance is not successful installation or runtime verification; Windows behavior is unchanged.

Legacy implicit monitoring remains available for a fully loaded, unchanged current revision with verified repository and discovery provenance and no pending monitoring request. Overlapping revision loads cannot stamp newer provenance onto older inputs or replace monitoring edits with stale responses. Explicit empty lists remain opt-outs; historical, edited, malformed, or unverifiable implicit settings are not silently treated as committed choices.
